# Repository guidance

## Conventions

- Keep the reusable API in `src/index.ts` and the thin executable adapter in `src/cli.ts`; the CLI never re-implements greeting logic, and it rejects unknown options before honouring `--help`.
- Publish only built artifacts: `exports`, `bin` and `files` in `package.json` point at `dist/`, which `npm run build` generates and nobody edits by hand.
- Tests are `node:test` files under `test/*.test.ts` that import `src/*.ts` directly (Node 22 type stripping); the unit command names every test file explicitly, so a new test file is added to `package.json`, `roadmap/roadmap.config.json` and `.github/greenfield-delivery.json` in the same commit as the behaviour it covers.
- Gates and their exact commands live in `roadmap/roadmap.config.json` and README §Commands; `lint` and `e2e` are declared absent (`none`) until real tooling exists.
- Documentation homes: product facts in `docs/PRD.md`, decisions in `docs/adr/`, style in `docs/CODE-STYLE.md`, the architecture index in `docs/architecture.md`, the CLI contract in `docs/ux-canon.md`. Link to a home instead of copying its content.
- Roadmap work goes through the installed zeroh-roadmap skills against the single root `roadmap/` (`roadmap.config.json` with its local `roadmap.config.schema.json`, `backlog.ts`, `phases/`); never create a second root or configuration, and never point consumer files at plugin-internal paths.

## Don't

- No runtime dependencies, framework runtime, external service, authentication, mobile target, deployment or product remote.
- No publishing: the package is private and UNLICENSED, and `release.provider` stays `none` in `.github/greenfield-delivery.json`.
- No invented design tokens or UI vocabulary; the only surface is CLI text (ADR 0002, `docs/ux-canon.md`).
- Do not hand-edit generated files (`dist/`, `reviews/changelog.json`, `package-lock.json`) or bypass the delivery lifecycle in `.github/workflows/`.
- Do not lower `baseline` floors in `.github/greenfield-delivery.json` to hide a regression; a baseline change needs `baselineApproval`.

## Generalize-forward

Extract a shared helper only when the same logic is needed by both the API and the CLI, or by two tests; a single use stays inline. New public behaviour is added to `src/index.ts` first and then exposed by `src/cli.ts`.

## Flag-first delivery

A behaviour change that alters existing output ships behind an explicit opt-in option (CLI flag or API parameter) whose default keeps the current behaviour; the flag is removed in the roadmap phase that makes the new behaviour the default.

/**
 * Reusable greeting API. The CLI in ./cli.ts is a thin adapter over this module.
 * Contract: docs/ux-canon.md §Interaction rules.
 */
export const DEFAULT_NAME = 'world'

/**
 * Build a greeting for `name`.
 * - `undefined` (or no argument) greets the default name, `world`.
 * - A blank name (empty or whitespace-only) is rejected with a TypeError.
 */
export function greet(name?: string): string {
  if (name === undefined) return `Hello, ${DEFAULT_NAME}!`
  if (typeof name !== 'string' || name.trim() === '') {
    throw new TypeError('greet(name): name must be a non-blank string')
  }
  return `Hello, ${name}!`
}

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Thin executable adapter over the greeting API (src/index.ts).
 * Contract: docs/ux-canon.md §Interaction rules.
 */
import { greet } from './index.ts'

const HELP_FLAGS = ['--help', '-h']

const USAGE = [
  'Usage: greenfield-proof [name]',
  '',
  'Print "Hello, <name>!" (default name: world).',
  '',
  'Options:',
  '  -h, --help  Print this usage and exit 0',
  '',
].join('\n')

interface Outcome {
  code: number
  stdout: string
  stderr: string
}

function run(argv: readonly string[]): Outcome {
  // Unknown options are rejected first, so they exit 1 even next to --help.
  const unknown = argv.find((arg) => arg.startsWith('-') && !HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))
  if (unknown !== undefined) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Unknown option: ${unknown}\n${USAGE}` }
  if (argv.some((arg) => HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))) return { code: 0, stdout: USAGE, stderr: '' }
  if (argv.length > 1) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Too many arguments: expected at most one name\n${USAGE}` }
  try {
    return { code: 0, stdout: `${greet(argv[0])}\n`, stderr: '' }
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
    return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `${message}\n${USAGE}` }
  }
}

const outcome = run(process.argv.slice(2))
process.stdout.write(outcome.stdout)
process.stderr.write(outcome.stderr)
process.exitCode = outcome.code

# UX canon

## Visual language

None. The product has no graphical surface; the only user interface is plain CLI text on stdout and stderr, with no colours, tokens, fonts, palette or spacing.

## Component vocabulary

- Greeting line: `Hello, <name>!` followed by a newline on stdout.
- Usage text: starts with `Usage: greenfield-proof [name]` and lists the options.
- Error line: one sentence on stderr, followed by the usage text.

## Interaction rules

| Invocation | stdout | stderr | exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `greenfield-proof` | `Hello, world!` | empty | 0 |
| `greenfield-proof Ada` | `Hello, Ada!` | empty | 0 |
| `greenfield-proof --help` or `-h` | usage text | empty | 0 |
| `greenfield-proof --unknown` | empty | `Unknown option: --unknown` + usage | 1 |
| `greenfield-proof --help --unknown` (any order) | empty | `Unknown option: --unknown` + usage | 1 |
| `greenfield-proof ''` or a whitespace-only name | empty | the `TypeError` message + usage | 1 |
| more than one name | empty | `Too many arguments` + usage | 1 |

Unknown options are checked before help, so an unknown option never exits 0. The API mirrors the CLI: `greet()` and `greet(undefined)` return `Hello, world!`, `greet(name)` returns `Hello, <name>!` verbatim, and blank names throw `TypeError`.

export const DEFAULT_NAME = 'world'

/**
 * Build a greeting for `name`.
 * - `undefined` (or no argument) greets the default name, `world`.
 * - A blank name (empty or whitespace-only) is rejected with a TypeError.
 */
export function greet(name?: string): string {
  if (name === undefined) return `Hello, ${DEFAULT_NAME}!`
  if (typeof name !== 'string' || name.trim() === '') {
    throw new TypeError('greet(name): name must be a non-blank string')
  }
  return `Hello, ${name}!`
}

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Thin executable adapter over the greeting API (src/index.ts).
 * Contract: docs/ux-canon.md §Interaction rules.
 */
import { greet } from './index.ts'

const HELP_FLAGS = ['--help', '-h']

const USAGE = [
  'Usage: greenfield-proof [name]',
  '',
  'Print "Hello, <name>!" (default name: world).',
  '',
  'Options:',
  '  -h, --help  Print this usage and exit 0',
  '',
].join('\n')

interface Outcome {
  code: number
  stdout: string
  stderr: string
}

function run(argv: readonly string[]): Outcome {
  // Unknown options are rejected first, so they exit 1 even next to --help.
  const unknown = argv.find((arg) => arg.startsWith('-') && !HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))
  if (unknown !== undefined) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Unknown option: ${unknown}\n${USAGE}` }
  if (argv.some((arg) => HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))) return { code: 0, stdout: USAGE, stderr: '' }
  if (argv.length > 1) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Too many arguments: expected at most one name\n${USAGE}` }
  try {
    return { code: 0, stdout: `${greet(argv[0])}\n`, stderr: '' }
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
    return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `${message}\n${USAGE}` }
  }
}

const outcome = run(process.argv.slice(2))
process.stdout.write(outcome.stdout)
process.stderr.write(outcome.stderr)
process.exitCode = outcome.code
